gretil-vaidya.citation: Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra, saṃkṣiptamātṛkā. GRETIL TEI edition, based on P. L. Vaidya (ed.), Mahāyāna-sūtra-saṃgrahaḥ, Part 1, Darbhanga: Mithila Institute, 1961 (Buddhist Sanskrit Texts 17), p. 97. Input: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Project.
gretil-vaidya.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (the e-text). Used only to verify the spelling of individual terms; no running text is copied into the app.

gretil-richards.citation: Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra, GRETIL TEI edition (legacy file prajnhsu.htm, input by John Richards; print source not stated).
gretil-richards.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Secondary witness only: its provenance is unstated and it contains typos (e.g. 'Āvalokiteśvaro', 'cāryāṃ', 'Tradhva').

mn1884.citation: F. Max Müller & Bunyiu Nanjio (eds.), The Ancient Palm-Leaves containing the Pragñâ-pâramitâ-hridaya-sûtra and the Ushnîsha-vigaya-dhâranî, with an appendix by G. Bühler. Anecdota Oxoniensia, Aryan Series, Vol. I, Part III. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1884. 'Shorter Text restored', pp. 48–50; Ziogon's romanized transliteration, pp. 17–22.
mn1884.license: Public domain (1884). archive.org marks the scan with the Public Domain Mark 1.0; the scan is the 1976 AMS reprint of the 1881–84 edition and includes Part III.
mn1884.status: Optional cross-check (CLAUDE.md §3.5). The edition is located, but individual spellings have not yet been checked against it: the restored text is set in Devanagari, which the OCR cannot read. Not a condition for review.iast.

dila-shh.citation: W. E. Soothill & L. Hodous, A Dictionary of Chinese Buddhist Terms (1937), DILA TEI P5 digital edition (from Charles Muller's DDB digitization, 2002–03).
dila-shh.license: license unconfirmed: the glossary page states no license, only the site footer 'DILA 2005/2026'. Cross-check reference only; not cited by any entry.

normalization: Spellings follow GRETIL's IAST normalization. Sandhi is undone and forms are reduced to stems for single terms (e.g. 'nāvidyā' → 'avidyā', 'cakṣurdhātur' → 'cakṣurdhātu'). Compounds are hyphenated at their members for readability. Phrase-level entries keep the attested sandhi. Müller's pre-IAST conventions (â, ri, g for j, etc.) are not used directly.
